scientific_question: Across independently dated East-Asian Cirsium lineage divergences, do historical climate state, short-window climate change or climate variability occupy recurring extreme regimes after node-age and regional uncertainty are propagated?
analysis_scope: lineage-diversification context only; this is not a capitulum-trait transition test and does not enter the manuscript by default

paleoclimate.resolution: 1 degree x 1 degree; 1 kyr; last 5 Myr
paleoclimate.selection_rule: Use every BIOCLIM variable supplied by the PALEO-PGEM-Series record; no variable is selected from any present-day trait-environment result.
paleoclimate.model_uncertainty_boundary: This exploratory atlas uses the public mean fields. PALEO-PGEM emulator/downscaling uncertainty is not propagated here, so any signal remains diagnostic until separately validated.

events.role: parent divergence context for the bounded orientation stem; ancestral region unresolved
representative Arenicola sister-lineage differentiation across the central Ryukyus/Miyako Strait
within-Taiwan sister differentiation temporal sequence diagnostic

excluded_contexts.reason: The 2.4 Ma founder event is a broad dispersal/radiation context with a 1.7-3.6 Ma interval and unresolved source-to-recipient paleolocation. It is retained as radiation background but excluded from this event-regime atlas.

age_uncertainty.interpretation: Deterministic age scenarios across published marginal intervals; not posterior samples and not equal-probability event ages.

univariate_estimands.level: regional median climate value at the candidate node age, percentile-ranked against the same region/background horizon
univariate_estimands.absolute_change: absolute difference between regional median climate at +/- half the fixed short window around the candidate node age, percentile-ranked against matched background centers
univariate_estimands.local_variability: temporal SD of the regional median climate within the fixed short window around the candidate node age, percentile-ranked against matched background centers

multivariate_estimands.method: Within each region/background, standardize all 17 BIOCLIM series, derive PCA, retain the minimum number of PCs explaining at least 95 percent of variance, whiten retained PC scores, and compute climate-state distance, short-window displacement magnitude and within-window multivariate variability.
multivariate_estimands.reason: Avoid treating correlated BIOCLIM variables as independent votes while retaining an exploratory all-climate view.

robustness_rules.univariate_tail: For a given event x metric x variable, require the same tail class across every allowed region scenario and both background horizons after propagating the full node-age grid. Low requires age-grid q95 <= 0.10; high requires q05 >= 0.90; otherwise unresolved.
robustness_rules.multivariate_high: For state distance, displacement or variability, require age-grid q05 >= 0.90 in every allowed region scenario and both background horizons; otherwise unresolved.
robustness_rules.common_context_candidate: Aggregate only the three group_representative events (Nipponocirsium, Arenicola, Sinocirsium). A domain is a descriptive recurring lineage-differentiation context if at least two of three representative clade groups independently pass the same robust class. Three of three is stronger. No p-value is assigned because these dated nodes and studies are not statistically independent replicates.

outputs.event_variable_long: all event x age x region x background x variable x metric scenario summaries
outputs.event_summary: robust event-level classes after age and region uncertainty
outputs.representative_group_summary: descriptive recurrence across three representative clade contexts

claim_boundary: This analysis concerns lineage differentiation context, not the timing or cause of a capitulum-trait transition.
Nested Nipponocirsium nodes are not counted as independent biological replicates; only one predeclared representative per broad clade group enters the cross-group recurrence summary.
Published node-age intervals are uncertainty bounds, not biological transition durations and not posterior samples.
Regional boxes are paleolocation sensitivity scenarios, not ancestral-area probabilities.
A recurring climate regime at lineage divergence would be a historical differentiation-context candidate, not evidence of natural selection or adaptation.
No result from this exploratory atlas is required to appear in the final manuscript.
A lineage-diversification context cannot be substituted for a missing capitulum-trait trigger.
